[
Xenograft Animal Models

Tumor volume growth delay studies. Immunocompromised NOD/SCID or Nude mice receive cell
line-matrigel mixture injection (subcutaneous).

][97]
[
Patient Derived Xenograft (PDX) Models

The patient derived xenografts combine the advantages of working with the cancer cells harvested
from a patient with the physiological relevance of an in vivo host.

][98]
[
Patient Chemosensitivity Xenograft Testing

Evaluate the efficacy of a panel of chemotherapy drugs for individual donor. Develop new therapeutic
agents optimized for individual donor.

][99]

Xenotransplantation of human tumor tissue into immunocompromised mice provides cancer-specific
xenograft models for pre-clinical drug development of anti-tumor therapies and novel oncology
medicines. We provide both patient derived xenograft services ([PDX Models][100]) and tumor
chemosensitivity xenograft testing services. Xenograft experiments based on [validated CDX xenograft
animal models][101] (cell line derived xenografts) are a potent research tool in oncology,
performing a critical task in evaluation of novel cancer therapies as part of the translation from
bench to clinic. Researchers utilize these services to identify anti-tumor activity of newly
developed therapeutic compounds and to characterize the direct involvement of specific proteins in
tumor growth control.

Xenotransplantation of human tumor tissue into immunocompromised mice provides cancer-specific
xenograft models for pre-clinical drug development of anti-tumor therapies and novel oncology
medicines. We provide both patient derived xenograft services ([PDX Models][100]) and tumor
chemosensitivity xenograft testing services. Xenograft experiments based on [validated CDX xenograft
animal models][101] (cell line derived xenografts) are a potent research tool in oncology,
performing a critical task in evaluation of novel cancer therapies as part of the translation from
bench to clinic. Researchers utilize these services to identify anti-tumor activity of newly
developed therapeutic compounds and to characterize the direct involvement of specific proteins in
tumor growth control.

Human tumor xenograft models are used for new drug discovery and development, and are extremely
useful tools in oncology. These models can be used for general treatment research and for
identifying the details of tumor growth and development. Xenograft models are also widely used for
personalized cancer treatment set up and tests, as their cancerous cells are similar to those of the
original tumor. Xenograft model techniques allow in vivo tests on human tumors, not on mouse tumors,
which may not have the same response on a particular drug or dose concentration.

Studies with xenotransplantation can be used to measure the activity of compounds based on the rate
of growth exhibited by the engrafted tumors. Experimental targets may be tumors that originate from
specific tissues such as breast, colon or lung. A multitude of tissue specific models exist and more
are being developed. Altogen Labs has the expertise to utilize these models and any new models as
they become available. In addition, we will work with the client to develop novel cancer models to
address the client’s needs. CDX model studies can be highly complex, starting with the selection of
appropriate animal model, appropriate tumorigenic cell line choice, administration method and the
complex analysis of tumor growth. We utilize our years of experience in xenotransplantation studies
in house at [Altogen Labs][189] to aid our clients in the planning and execution of experiments.

Researchers investigating the role of specific proteins or gene products in regulating tumor growth
will benefit from Altogen Labs xenograft services as well as [generation of stable cell lines][190]
services. Cell lines genetically engineered to ectopically express proteins, tumor suppressors or
oncogenes can be used in xenograft studies to directly test the role of specific proteins in
regulating tumor growth.

Cell lines can be engineered to constitutively express proteins or to inducibly express proteins.
Genetically engineered cells are not limited to ectopic expression of proteins but can also be used
for expression of inhibitory RNAs (RNAi). Altogen Labs offers [stable RNAi][191] cell line
development for gene knockdown experiments. Both constitutive and inducible expression systems can
be employed in xenografting studies.

In addition, Altogen Labs has a unique [protein expression detection service][192] (automated and
quantitative) that facilitates biomarker validation of xenograft tumors. The WES protein expression
system of immunodetection can be used to analyze xenograft biopsy samples with large panels of
antibodies. We also provide an array of other mRNA and protein expression services (qRT-PCR, ELISA,
Flow Cytometry, Western Blot, etc).

Animal handling and maintenance at the Altogen Labs facility is IACUC regulated compliant to GLP
standards. Detailed experimental procedures, health reports and data reports provided. Additional
services includes collection of tissues, histology, isolation of DNA/RNA and analysis of gene
expression. Furthermore, animal facilities have the flexibility to use specialized food or water
systems for inducible gene expression systems.

## *In Vivo* Xenograft CRO

Our *in vivo* contract research services (biology CRO services) feature a variety of custom services
utilizing xenograft mouse models. Xenograft models are used to assess the effectiveness of test
compounds against a range of cancers at various stages. These test articles are tested on staged
tumor growths of subcutaneous or orthotopic engrafted tumors. Our xenograft services measure the
efficacy of drugs using immunocompromised rodents to evaluate the potency of novel anti-cancer
compunds. We strive to continually expand and improve upon our CRO services. We provide *in vivo*
xenograft services to develop treatments for cancer, diabetes, infection diseases, obesity,
immunology and inflammation. Our expert staff can provide you with comprehensive experiment
procedures, health reports and related experimental data.

identifying the details of tumor growth and development. Xenograft models are also widely used for
personalized cancer treatment set up and tests, as their cancerous cells are similar to those of the
original tumor. Xenograft model techniques allow in vivo tests on human tumors, not on mouse tumors,
which may not have the same response on a particular drug or dose concentration.

Studies with xenotransplantation can be used to measure the activity of compounds based on the rate
of growth exhibited by the engrafted tumors. Experimental targets may be tumors that originate from
specific tissues such as breast, colon or lung. A multitude of tissue specific models exist and more
are being developed. Altogen Labs has the expertise to utilize these models and any new models as
they become available. In addition, we will work with the client to develop novel cancer models to
address the client’s needs. CDX model studies can be highly complex, starting with the selection of
appropriate animal model, appropriate tumorigenic cell line choice, administration method and the
complex analysis of tumor growth. We utilize our years of experience in xenotransplantation studies
in house at [Altogen Labs][189] to aid our clients in the planning and execution of experiments.

Researchers investigating the role of specific proteins or gene products in regulating tumor growth
will benefit from Altogen Labs xenograft services as well as [generation of stable cell lines][190]
services. Cell lines genetically engineered to ectopically express proteins, tumor suppressors or
oncogenes can be used in xenograft studies to directly test the role of specific proteins in
regulating tumor growth.

Cell lines can be engineered to constitutively express proteins or to inducibly express proteins.
Genetically engineered cells are not limited to ectopic expression of proteins but can also be used
for expression of inhibitory RNAs (RNAi). Altogen Labs offers [stable RNAi][191] cell line
development for gene knockdown experiments. Both constitutive and inducible expression systems can
be employed in xenografting studies.

In addition, Altogen Labs has a unique [protein expression detection service][192] (automated and
quantitative) that facilitates biomarker validation of xenograft tumors. The WES protein expression
system of immunodetection can be used to analyze xenograft biopsy samples with large panels of
antibodies. We also provide an array of other mRNA and protein expression services (qRT-PCR, ELISA,
Flow Cytometry, Western Blot, etc).

Animal handling and maintenance at the Altogen Labs facility is IACUC regulated compliant to GLP
standards. Detailed experimental procedures, health reports and data reports provided. Additional
services includes collection of tissues, histology, isolation of DNA/RNA and analysis of gene
expression. Furthermore, animal facilities have the flexibility to use specialized food or water
systems for inducible gene expression systems.

Our *in vivo* contract research services (biology CRO services) feature a variety of custom services
utilizing xenograft mouse models. Xenograft models are used to assess the effectiveness of test
compounds against a range of cancers at various stages. These test articles are tested on staged
tumor growths of subcutaneous or orthotopic engrafted tumors. Our xenograft services measure the
efficacy of drugs using immunocompromised rodents to evaluate the potency of novel anti-cancer
compunds. We strive to continually expand and improve upon our CRO services. We provide *in vivo*
xenograft services to develop treatments for cancer, diabetes, infection diseases, obesity,
